sources.verification: Model lists are public and were fetched, not recalled. Shapes come from each vendor's own task/metadata fields; anything guessed is marked in shape_source.
sources.cloudflare_input_keys: Shape gives the endpoint, not the payload: Cloudflare's env.AI.run input object key varies per model even inside one shape — {messages} for chat models, {prompt} for text-to-text and image, {text} for embeddings and some TTS, {audio} for ASR, {query,contexts} for rerankers. Confirm the key on the model's docs page before wiring one.

chat.why: Text in, text out. One body covers every chat-capable id on both sides, so a new model is an id swap.

responses.why: Mixed media in one request, so a photo or a PDF is not a special case in the router.

embed.why: Vectors out. Dimensions differ per model, so the model id must be stored beside the vector.

rerank.why: Ordering only. Scores come back, so you keep your own records and re-sort instead of trusting its text.

image.why: Binary out, so it can never be a chat turn; the card has to carry the image.

response.openrouter: job id at once; poll status, then an output URL

video.why: Asynchronous. Never block a Worker request on it: needs a job record plus poll or webhook.

stt.why: Audio in, text out. The one shape whose input is not text.

tts.why: Raw bytes out: must not be JSON-decoded, and on Cloudflare it arrives base64 inside JSON.
